provenance: Merged from two independent drafts (A: the 16 project copy, B: the 01 project copy; the files are byte-identical) by subagents that read only the page and its pubspec, with no access to SKILL.md, references/, the scenario files or any past report. Merging rule, applied without exception: an item is required only if both drafts marked it required; a disagreement, or an item only one draft found, is optional. Root causes a draft split or joined differently were merged by root cause. Line numbers checked against the file. "drafts" names the source items.
excluded: Order, Item, User, OrderApi, UserApi and UserCache are defined nowhere and pubspec.yaml declares no flutter dependency, so the project cannot analyse as given. Both drafts treated this as a property of the fixture, not a defect in the file, and it is not an item.
reviewQuestions: GT-15 (cancelled order shows Awaiting payment) was found by one draft only, so it is optional. If it is a planted defect, it should be required.
GT-01 and GT-02 are both required and close: teardown vs a mounted guard after await. A finding naming only setState-after-dispose may fairly be credited to either.
Scenario 16 asks to fix a crash. GT-34 (late order + loading bool, LateInitializationError) is optional here; if the planted crash is that one, it should be required for 16.

items.claim: The State has no dispose(): the stream subscription is never cancelled and the ScrollController never disposed, so both outlive the page and the subscription keeps calling setState on an unmounted State; the "// no dispose" comment records the gap instead of closing it.
load() calls setState after awaiting fetchOrder with no mounted check, so a page popped before the fetch completes gets setState on a disposed State.
The catch swallows every error with "// ignore": a failed fetch leaves loading true, so the user sees an endless spinner, and nothing is logged.
Other async failures have no handler: the stream is listened to without onError, and the button fires getUser as an unawaited future, so their errors are unhandled.
The 'Reload profile' button calls getUser and discards the result without setState, so pressing it changes nothing on screen.
getUser reads as a pure query but also writes to UserCache; the name hides the side effect.

items.location: order_summary_page.dart:17, order_summary_page.dart:24, order_summary_page.dart:37, order_summary_page.dart:42, order_summary_page.dart:48, order_summary_page.dart:55
items.claim: Cryptic abbreviations force the reader to decode them: sub, o, d, e, tmp, t.
Names that say nothing about intent: load, describe and render are generic verbs, discount is a noun for a computation, loading is a bool without an is/has prefix.
getTotal() looks like a query but writes _cachedTotal, a field nothing reads: dead state and a hidden side effect in a getter-like method.
The premium discount threshold 100 and rate 0.1 are unexplained business literals.
By its own comment the discount rule is duplicated in invoice_service.dart, so two copies of one business rule can drift; the comment records the duplication instead of removing it.

The State class fetches data, writes a cache, computes prices and discounts, formats dates and statuses and builds the whole UI: several reasons to change, and pure logic that cannot be tested without a widget.
OrderApi, UserApi and UserCache are constructed inline, fresh on each call, so they cannot be injected or replaced in tests.
describe() nests if/else three levels deep where guard clauses would read flat.
describe() returns 'Awaiting payment' for every status but paid, so a cancelled order shows 'Cancelled' and 'Awaiting payment' side by side.
Status is stringly typed: the literals 'paid', 'pending', 'cancelled' are compared in two methods with no enum or exhaustive switch, so a new status or a typo falls through silently.
build() is about 118 lines assembling header, status, item rows, premium banner, totals and action in one method instead of composing named widgets.
The label/value row (Padding > Row > Text, Spacer, Text) is copy-pasted for Subtotal, Discount and Total, and the item row repeats the same shape.
render() is a widget-building helper method rather than a widget class, so it gets no const construction or rebuild boundary of its own.
render() takes a boolean flag that switches between two outputs, so it does two things and the call render(order, false) is unreadable.
Unreachable branches: render's compact branch never runs because the only caller passes false, and describe()'s null branch never runs because its only caller passes a non-null order.

items.location: order_summary_page.dart:99, order_summary_page.dart:118, order_summary_page.dart:138, order_summary_page.dart:160, order_summary_page.dart:166, order_summary_page.dart:178
items.claim: Font sizes, colours and gaps are raw literals in inline styles instead of theme text styles or spacing constants.
Rows are built by mutating a list with add() in a loop and an if, then spread in, where collection-for and collection-if would declare them in place.
The subtotal is recomputed by walking the items several times per build: discount() calls getTotal() twice and is itself called twice.
Two comments restate the code that follows and add nothing.
A commented-out older total calculation is left in the method body.
A vague TODO above build() says neither what to fix nor why, and names no owner or reference.
The private widget _SectionGap is never used: dead code.
OrderSnapshot compares and hashes items by list identity, so snapshots with equal contents are unequal.
OrderSnapshot is a model class in a page file, unused here.
The order is loaded from both a watch stream and a one-shot fetch, both writing order and loading, so a stale fetch can overwrite a newer stream value and the fetch is redundant.
One state is encoded as a late Order plus a separate loading bool; only convention keeps build() from reading order before assignment, and a slip becomes a LateInitializationError.
Dates are hand-formatted d/m/y with no padding or locale.
Money is a double and formatted inconsistently: item prices interpolated raw, totals with toStringAsFixed(2).

items.claim: User-facing strings are hard-coded rather than localised.
The avatar NetworkImage has no error or placeholder handling.
While loading, build returns a bare Center with no Scaffold or AppBar, so the page chrome appears only when data arrives.
The ScrollController is attached but never read or driven, a resource that only adds disposal work.
formatDate, statusLabel and describe are pure functions kept as State instance methods, which makes them look stateful and keeps them from unit tests.
Data fetching and state live in the StatefulWidget; choosing a state-management approach is an architecture decision.
